purpose: rescale-invariant shape tests along the size and concentration axes, on the working sample the calibration is fitted on (the review of 2 October 2026, P-17)
method: src/test_shape_invariance.py's statistics: row-level Kruskal-Wallis on quartile ranks; k-sample Anderson-Darling on the quartiles, each centred by its median and scaled by its IQR; Bowley skewness, the tail-skew ratio and Moors kurtosis, compared top less bottom quartile and as a slope across deciles, each with a 95% interval from a cluster bootstrap over syndicates
anderson_darling_p_note: scipy reports the k-sample Anderson-Darling p within [0.001, 0.25]: 0.25 is its cap, not an estimate
row_test_note: Kruskal-Wallis and Anderson-Darling are ordinary row-level SciPy tests; within-syndicate dependence may miscalibrate them, and estimated group median/IQR standardisation can alter the Anderson-Darling reference
bootstrap_sign_note: legacy bootstrap p is twice the smaller observed-bootstrap sign fraction without null centering, not an established null-calibrated p-value
group_shape_note: each group mixes observations with potentially different conditional scales; pooled shape can change with the scale mix even if conditional shape is invariant
reading: The legacy no_drift flag is true when all intended groups enter the row-level Anderson-Darling comparison, its p is at or above the line, and every interval covers zero. This descriptive threshold rule does not establish invariance; the row-level p may be miscalibrated under panel dependence.
